channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims to Boost Oil Product Exports to $1.5 Billion by 2028
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to increase its oil product exports to $1.5 billion by 2028, a 60% rise from current levels. The strategy involves expanding production, securing raw materials, developing logistics, and increasing foreign market presence. Oil product export revenue has grown fivefold in five seasons, reaching $1.232 billion.

item.title: Khorezm Region Allocates 1 Billion Sums for Women's Entrepreneurship Development
item.description: The Khorezm region has allocated 1 billion sums in grants to support the business initiatives of 25 women as part of the 'Rural Entrepreneurship Development' project. The project, in collaboration with the Ministry of Employment and Poverty Reduction and the World Bank, aims to boost rural entrepreneurship and income generation.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan Leaders Hold Phone Conversation
item.description: The leaders of Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan held a phone conversation, discussing the successful chairmanship of Turkmenistan in regional meetings and the strengthening of bilateral strategic partnership. They emphasized expanding trade, industrial cooperation, and joint projects in energy, transport, and agriculture, as well as cultural exchanges.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Sports Medicine Center Gains International Recognition as FIMS Partner
item.description: The Republican Scientific-Practical Center of Sports Medicine in Uzbekistan has become an official partner of the International Federation of Sports Medicine (FIMS). This partnership grants international recognition to diagnoses made by Uzbek specialists and opens opportunities for collaboration with global sports medicine organizations.

item.title: Restaurant Owner in Aktobe Region Pays $200,000 Tenge for Food Poisoning Incident
item.description: A restaurant owner in Kandyagash, Aktobe region, has been ordered to pay 200,000 tenge in moral damages to a guest who suffered food poisoning. The guest was among 188 people affected by an outbreak at the "Tumar" restaurant. The restaurant was operating without a permit, and food samples revealed infectious agents.

item.title: Taliban's Rule Creates More Opponents Than Supporters, Alienating Ideological Allies
item.description: The Taliban's governance is reportedly multiplying opponents by alienating even those with shared ideological foundations. Figures like Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, despite a history of Islamist politics, are now challenging the Taliban's legitimacy and methods. This suggests a "repulsive force" stemming from ethnic power monopolies and refusal to accept Afghanistan's pluralism.

item.title: Taliban Detain 13 Workers in Parwan; Whereabouts Unknown After 26 Days
item.description: Local sources in Parwan province report that 13 workers were detained by the Taliban 26 days ago in Hanrowa Bala village. Their current whereabouts remain unknown, and local officials have provided no clear information despite inquiries from community elders and representatives.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Belgium Foreign Ministries Agree on Three-Year Cooperation Plan
item.description: Kazakhstan and Belgium's foreign ministries have signed a cooperation roadmap for 2027-2029. The plan aims to boost political dialogue, inter-agency contacts, and joint initiatives. The agreement was reached in Astana during a meeting between Kazakh Deputy Foreign Minister Yerzhan Ashikbayev and Belgian official Theodora Gentzis.

item.title: Nine Sentenced in Astana Apartment Fraud Case Involving Over 5 Billion Tenge
item.description: Nine individuals have been sentenced in Astana for perpetrating apartment fraud, posing as representatives of construction companies. They collected money from citizens seeking to buy apartments in residential complexes, creating fraudulent booking agreements. The total damages incurred by 135 victims amount to over 5.36 billion tenge, with no compensation yet provided.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Enhance State Procurement System Reforms
item.description: Uzbekistan is set to improve its state procurement system as part of reforms aimed at fostering competition and efficient budget spending. Changes to the Law "On State Procurement" are planned, focusing on removing local producer preferences, increasing transparency, and strengthening parliamentary oversight. Regional complaint commissions will also be established.

item.title: Astana Announces Grants Up to 5 Million Tenge for Social Entrepreneurs
item.description: Astana has launched an open competition for state grants for social entrepreneurship entities, with a maximum funding amount of 5 million tenge. Eligible participants include social entrepreneurs registered in the relevant registry and finalists of the "One Village – One Product" program. Applications will be accepted electronically via the kezekte.kz platform between October 15-20, 2026.

item.title: Almaty Police Warn of 'Trap Date' Robbery Scheme Targeting Young Men
item.description: Almaty police have identified and prosecuted four groups involved in a 'trap date' robbery scheme this year. The modus operandi involves women meeting men online, luring them to apartments where accomplices pose as relatives to extort money and rob victims. Authorities urge caution with online acquaintances and advise immediate reporting of threats.

item.title: Dogs from Shelter Whose Owner Was Murdered Relocated in Almaty Region
item.description: Dogs from the 'Tvardovsky Dom' shelter, whose owner Vladimir Teplyakov was murdered, have been moved to a new location. Volunteers from the 'Dvoryanskoye Sobraniye' shelter in Almaty facilitated the relocation, citing immense effort and cost. The dogs are now safe and cared for, but the search for new homes continues, requiring financial aid and public support.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economic Growth Faces Challenges in Tax System
item.description: Kyrgyzstan boasts the fastest-growing economy in the EAEU, with GDP increasing by 11.1% in 2025. Despite favorable tax rates and business conditions, the country's tax administration system presents challenges. Tax revenues grew significantly in the first nine months of 2026, but underlying issues may hinder predictable business growth.

item.title: Concert Organizer Faces Five Years in Prison for Shymkent Stampede
item.description: An investigation is ongoing into a mass stampede at a Kairat Nurtas concert in Shymkent. The organizer has been detained and faces charges of violating safety requirements. Penalties could include a fine of up to 5,000 MCI or imprisonment for up to five years. An 18-year-old girl remains in serious condition.

item.title: Kazakh Citizens Advised on Safety Amid Saudi Arabia Airport Attacks
item.description: Kazakh citizens in Saudi Arabia are advised to exercise increased caution and follow local authorities' instructions due to recent airport attacks. They should avoid unnecessary travel to airports, verify flight statuses, and refrain from visiting crowded places. In emergencies, citizens should contact the Kazakh embassies in Riyadh or Jeddah.

item.title: VietJet Air Launches Hanoi-Almaty-Prague Route with Two Weekly Flights
item.description: VietJet Air has introduced a new route connecting Hanoi, Almaty, and Prague, operating twice weekly. The inaugural flight carried approximately 200 Kazakh citizens to Prague. The airline utilizes Airbus A330-300 aircraft, and passengers can purchase tickets for the Prague-Almaty segment.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry Issues Warning to Citizens in Saudi Arabia Amidst Airport Attacks
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has issued a statement to its citizens in Saudi Arabia following attacks on airports. The ministry advises strict adherence to safety measures, avoiding airports unless necessary, and refraining from visiting crowded places. Citizens facing emergencies are urged to contact the Kazakh Embassy in Riyadh or the Consulate General in Jeddah.

item.title: Nobel Prize in Economics Awarded for Work on Inflation Control and Crisis Mitigation
item.description: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics to American economists Robert Hall and Michael Woodford for their work on the microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilization. Their research has significantly improved governments' and central banks' ability to implement stabilization policies, aiding in controlling inflation and preventing overheating.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Seeks Pakistan's Help Amid Depleting Air Defense Missiles Against Houthi Attacks
item.description: Saudi Arabia has requested military assistance from Pakistan to defend against Houthi attacks, as the Kingdom's air defense missile supplies are reportedly running low. The United States is not providing the requested military aid to the Saudi prince. This situation highlights the kingdom's vulnerability in its ongoing conflict.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Host 2027 CIS Summit in Bukhara; Strengthens International Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan will host the 2027 CIS Summit in Bukhara, with Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan as co-chairs, according to the CIS Secretary General. Foreign media, including TASS and Trend, highlight Uzbekistan's expanding international cooperation, economic development, and cultural heritage. The country also discussed 46 joint projects with the UK.

item.title: Uzbekistan Accelerates AI Integration into State Policy and Economy by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan has made digitalization a key state policy, integrating AI into strategies and services. The 'Digital Uzbekistan-2030' program and 'IT Park' initiatives have boosted the sector. State sources report Uzbekistan leads Central Asia in AI readiness, aiming to become a major AI user country by 2030.

item.title: Affluent Kazakh Families Voluntarily Renounce Social Payments Amid Means-Testing Introduction
item.description: Following news that some state benefits in Kazakhstan will now be means-tested, affluent families have begun voluntarily refusing social payments. Social media shows citizens stating they can support their families independently and believe support should prioritize those in genuine need. Entrepreneurs and fathers like Asen Zhaksylykov and Nurlan Minaydarov have publicly renounced benefits, emphasizing self-reliance and contributing to Kazakhstan's future.

item.title: Astana Court Sentences Nine Individuals for Fraudulent Apartment Sales Totaling 5.36 Billion Tenge
item.description: Nine people in Astana have been sentenced to 5 to 10 years in prison for fraud involving the fictitious sale of apartments in residential complexes. The group defrauded 135 victims of over 5.14 billion tenge through fake booking agreements and an additional 228 million tenge from reselling apartments in a building under construction.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports Significant Reduction in Crimes Against Children and by Minors
item.description: Kazakhstan has seen a 45% decrease in particularly grave crimes against children and a 10% reduction in sexual offenses against minors, according to Vice President Yerlan Karin. Crimes committed by minors also dropped by 10%. These improvements are attributed to legislative measures, including the 2024 law on women's rights and child safety, aimed at protecting children and enhancing education and healthcare.

item.title: Yandex Service Outage in Kazakhstan Disrupts Taxi and Delivery Services
item.description: A widespread outage of the Yandex service on October 11th left thousands of taxi drivers and couriers in Kazakhstan without work. The disruption, attributed to Ukrainian attacks on Russian data centers, also caused taxi prices to surge and led to public concern. While Yandex acknowledged the technical issue, a timeline for full restoration was not provided. Experts suggest this highlights the risks of over-reliance on a single service provider.

item.title: Foreign National Sentenced for Illegally Crossing Kazakhstan's Border
item.description: A foreign national who illegally crossed Kazakhstan's border after deserting his military service in Russia has been sentenced. The court ordered his deportation and a five-year ban from entering Kazakhstan. He was found guilty of illegally crossing the state border without passing through border control.

item.title: Pakistan Claims Over 20,000 Terrorists, Including TTP Members, Sheltering in Afghanistan
item.description: Pakistan's Information Minister stated that over 20,000 terrorists, including 6,000 TTP members, are harbored in Afghanistan. He alleged these individuals receive training in safe havens on Afghan territory and urged the Taliban to prevent terrorist activities, a claim denied by Taliban officials.

item.title: Kazakh Citizens in Saudi Arabia Advised on Safety Measures Amidst Attacks
item.description: Kazakh citizens in Saudi Arabia are advised to avoid airports unless necessary and postpone non-urgent travel due to attacks on civilian infrastructure. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs urges adherence to local authorities' instructions, avoidance of crowds, and monitoring official communications.

item.title: Kazakhstan Adopts 11 Laws to Protect Children's Rights Over Three Years
item.description: Kazakhstan has enacted 11 laws aimed at safeguarding children's rights and interests in the past three years, including a key law on women's rights and child safety passed in 2024. This has led to a decrease in severe crimes against children and crimes committed by minors. The country is also focusing on supporting children in difficult situations, with over 186,000 messages and 6,700 calls received by a child helpline.

item.title: Serious Crimes Against Children Decreased by 45%, Reports Yerlan Karin
item.description: The number of particularly serious crimes against children in Kazakhstan has decreased by 45%, according to Vice President Yerlan Karin. He chaired a meeting on implementing presidential initiatives for child welfare, including the "Children of Kazakhstan" concept for 2026-2030. Over $2.5 billion has been allocated to over 7 million children via the "National Fund for Children" program.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Fund Allocates Over $2.5 Billion to More Than 7 Million Children
item.description: Kazakhstan's presidential program "National Fund for Children" has disbursed over $2.5 billion to more than 7 million children in three years. This initiative is part of a broader strategy to protect children's rights, ensure their safety, improve education, and provide social support. The program also coincides with the construction of 1,342 schools for over a million students in the last seven years.

item.title: Doniyor Qodirov Appointed Acting Governor of Sirdaryo Region
item.description: Doniyor Qodirov has been appointed acting governor of the Sirdaryo region. Previously, he served as the head of the Department for Public Security and Rule of Law within the Presidential Administration. This appointment follows the previous governor's transition to a new role as First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Education.

item.title: Doniyor Qodirov Appointed Acting Governor of Sirdaryo Region
item.description: Doniyor Baxtiyorovich Qodirov has been appointed acting governor of the Sirdaryo region, as announced by presidential press secretary Sherzod Asadov. Qodirov previously headed the Presidential Administration's Department for Public Security and Rule of Law since July 2025. Before that, he served as an advisor on coordinating law enforcement activities.

item.title: Botir Kudratkhodjayev Appointed New Defense Minister of Uzbekistan
item.description: Botir Kudratkhodjayev has been appointed as the new Defense Minister of Uzbekistan by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Kudratkhodjayev, a Major General, previously served as the First Deputy Interior Minister. He also led the Ministry of Emergency Situations and held various prosecutor positions before his current appointment, replacing Lieutenant General Shuhrat Kholmukhamedov.

item.title: Kremlin Rejects Ukraine's 60-Day Ceasefire Proposal for Elections
item.description: The Kremlin has rejected Ukraine's proposal for a 60-day ceasefire to hold presidential elections, stating it would allow Ukraine to regroup for further conflict. Russia might consider a one-day pause only on the election day itself, if elections are scheduled. Ukraine previously suggested this for campaign and voting conditions.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan Leaders Discuss Strategic Partnership via Phone Call
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held a phone conversation with Turkmenistan's Gurbanguli Berdimuhamedov. During the call, both leaders positively noted the consistently developing and practically enriching strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. The discussion focused on strengthening bilateral ties and cooperation.

item.title: UNICEF Provided Health Services to Over 6 Million Afghans in August
item.description: UNICEF announced it delivered essential health services to 6.6 million people across Afghanistan in August. Services were provided through 2,390 fixed and 16 mobile health centers. During the same period, 149,476 people received safe drinking water, and 135,164 gained access to sanitation. Nutrition and health information was given to 433,568 individuals.

item.title: Iran Reports Fourfold Increase in Synthetic Drug Seizures Near Afghanistan Border
item.description: Iranian officials reported a fourfold increase in the seizure of synthetic drugs along the Razavi Khorasan Province border with Afghanistan during the first six months of the current year compared to last year. Officials seized 1.5 tonnes of narcotics, including opium, heroin, and industrial drugs, with crystal methamphetamine being a significant portion.

item.title: Pakistan's Foreign Minister Urges Taliban to Act Against Terrorist Groups
item.description: Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar has called on the Taliban to take concrete, verifiable, and irreversible steps against the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan and other terrorist groups. Dar stressed that Afghan territory must not be used for terrorist attacks against Pakistan or other countries, accusing India of supporting such groups.
